readings.commitment: Large-scale social coordination is achieved through authoritative institutions that claim the standing right to bind members and adjudicate their disputes
readings.delta: Moderate suppression (rival coordination modes subordinated to authority); beneficiary is office-holders and those with institutional access; victim set is the politically marginal; extractiveness moderate (compliance and revenue extraction by standing apparatus)

readings.commitment: Large-scale social coordination is achieved through voluntary exchange under price signals, with authority needed only to police the perimeter of contract
readings.delta: Low formal suppression (exit nominally free); beneficiary is asset-holders and intermediaries; victim set is those without endowments to trade; extractiveness varies with market power concentration

readings.commitment: Large-scale social coordination is achieved through extended webs of kin obligation and inherited reciprocity that precede and outlast any formal authority
readings.delta: High suppression of non-kin alternatives (obligation is ascribed, not chosen); beneficiary is lineage elders; victim set is junior and out-marrying members; extractiveness low in resources, high in life-course control

readings.commitment: Large-scale social coordination is achieved through shared ritual and sacralized consensus that makes defection cognitively unavailable rather than punishable
readings.delta: Very high suppression at the level of imagination (alternatives unthinkable, not forbidden); beneficiary is ritual specialists; victim set is heterodox members; extractiveness low and diffuse

readings.commitment: Governing authority is constituted and limited by a higher law that binds the governors themselves and survives any particular holder of power
readings.delta: Suppression redirected onto rulers (the constraint constrains the constrainer); beneficiary is the governed as a class; victim set is would-be absolute power-holders; extractiveness low by design, policed by entrenchment

readings.commitment: Governing authority is the unmediated will of a ruler whose commands are law because of who issues them, not because of any prior authorization
readings.delta: Maximal suppression of institutional alternatives; beneficiary is the ruler and the apparatus personally loyal to him; victim set is everyone outside the patronage circle; extractiveness high and arbitrary

readings.commitment: Governing authority is delegated from the divine order, and political obligation is a species of religious obligation administered by those who interpret the sacred law
readings.delta: High suppression presented as cosmic necessity (disobedience is sin, not crime); beneficiary is the interpreting clerisy; victim set is religious minorities and heterodox believers; extractiveness moderate, legitimated as offering

readings.commitment: Governing authority is the accumulated weight of immemorial custom, which no living ruler made and no living ruler may remake
readings.delta: Suppression by inertia rather than enforcement (the new is presumptively illegitimate); beneficiary is whoever the existing custom already favors; victim set is those custom subordinates; extractiveness low but frozen in place

readings.commitment: Governing authority is exercised by the assembled citizens themselves, and any delegation of that authority is a usurpation to be minimized
readings.delta: Low suppression of voice, high suppression of insulation (no counter-majoritarian shelter); beneficiary is the mobilized majority; victim set is persistent minorities; extractiveness tracks majority appetite
